question: Why did the McDonald brothers cut their drive-in menu from about 25 items to 9 in 1948?
answer: To turn a kitchen into an assembly line. With a handful of items, each worker could do one job: grill, dress, fry, shake. Carhops were dropped and customers queued at a window, so the hamburger's price could fall from 30 cents to 15. The menu shrank so the line could run.
move: Fewer choices can make everything else faster and cheaper.
ask: Which of my options could I drop so the rest runs better?
reference: Love, McDonald's: Behind the Arches, Bantam Books, 1986
